reader.requirement: When qualification leaves several objects, at most one may be local to B; then B's own object wins, else the object of A, else that of the next containing program outward, for data-names, condition-names, file-names, record-names and report-names.

reader.notes: 3a (I Y=INY, own FD F, own TOT=77), 3b1 (I X=MID, I C=FALSE, I TOT=55 from the middle program), 3b2 (3 X=OUX, J Z=OUZ) and the 'no more than one local' refusal (scopeamb, 3 declarations) all hold. The inheritance-time hiding of a sum counter by B's own data-name gives the right 3a answer for an unqualified reference; its error for a QUALIFIED one is GR1's finding.

refuter.evidence: The reader probed same-class duplicates (data/data, condition/condition, file/file, sum counter/data) and the B-data vs A-file pair, but not the report-name class against another class. §1985:X.1.3.8 makes the rule cross-class: 'a program's reference to such a name, even when it is a different type of user-defined word, is to the object which that program describes', and GR3a 'If the name is declared in program B, the object in program B is the referenced object'. Probe xrpt1.cob (container: FD RPF GLOBAL REPORT IS R1; RD R1 GLOBAL; contained XR1I: 01 R1 PIC X VALUE 'L'; INITIATE R1 / GENERATE DET / TERMINATE R1): --std 85 EXIT 0, prints 'I R1=L / I DONE' and xr1.rpt holds '5': the INITIATE R1 in XR1I reached the container's report though XR1I's R1 is a data-name (expected: refused, R1 there names XR1I's data item). Probe xrpt2.cob (container 01 XR PIC X GLOBAL; contained XR2I declares its own RD XR; MOVE 'B' TO XR in XR2I): --std 85 EXIT 0, prints 'I XR=B / O XR=B': the MOVE wrote the container's GLOBAL data item though XR in XR2I names XR2I's report (expected: refused). Control xfile1.cob (container GLOBAL FD F, contained 01 F; OPEN OUTPUT F): refused COBOL1639 at 22 and 25, so the data/file pair is right (PB5786 landed) and only the report-name arm is missing. Code: SymbolTable.Reports.cs#InheritReport hides an inherited report only when _visibleReports already holds the spelling (`if (!_visibleReports.TryAdd(Key(report.Name), report)) return false;`), i.e. only an own REPORT of the spelling hides it, never an own data-, condition- or file-name; and SymbolTable.cs#NearestDeclaringData asks NearerEntryHides, NearerConditionNameHides and Declarations.NearerFileNameHides but no nearer report-name. At --std 2023 both probes behave identically (xrpt1-002, xrpt2-002: EXIT 0, same output), cause b. kb/Work: PB5786 (landed, file-name arm) lists 'an own index-name or report-name against a container's GLOBAL data-name or file-name' as an unprobed lead; no note owns it. Citations: OK §1985:X.1.3.8 ('even when it is a different type of user-defined word'); OK §1985:X.1.3.8.2 GR3a ('If the name is declared in program B, the object in program B is the referenced object'); OK §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.1 ('condition-names, data-names, and record-names' and report-names are separate disjoint sets, so only the scope rule decides).
